query: Oracle OCI AI pipeline FY2027 earnings call
normalized: ai call earnings fy2027 oci oracle pipeline

output.content:
**Oracle OCI AI pipeline — Q1 FY2027 earnings-call takeaway (reported September 10, 2026):** Oracle characterized demand as capacity-constrained rather than demand-constrained: OCI cloud-infrastructure revenue rose 121% year over year to $7.4 billion, while the company deployed 850 megawatts of AI capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs during the quarter. [[1]]

**Contracted pipeline/backlog:** Remaining performance obligations (RPO) reached **$664 billion**, increasing **$26 billion sequentially**; management said it expects approximately half of RPO to convert to sales in the next 36 months. [[2, 3]]

**New AI bookings:** Oracle said it closed **more than $30 billion** of additional AI contracts in Q1. [[3]] Management stressed that these bookings generally used customer prepayments, customer-owned hardware, supplier financing, or similar structures, so they should not require *incremental Oracle cash*—but they can still entail capital expenditure. [[3, 1]]

**Capacity and pricing evidence:** GPU utilization was **97.9%**, and Oracle said capacity coming up for renewal was being resold at a **20% premium**, supporting the view that OCI’s near-term bottleneck is bringing power, data centers, and GPUs online rather than winning contracts. [[4, 3]]

**FY2027 outlook:** Management raised full-year revenue guidance to at least **$90 billion**—over **34%** growth—and guided to **$8.10** of non-GAAP EPS, explicitly expecting OCI growth to accelerate through the balance of FY2027 as additional RPO converts into revenue. [[3]]

**Investment implication:** The pipeline is unusually visible and large, but execution and financing remain the core risks: Q1 capital expenditures were about **$28 billion**, while Oracle retained FY2027 gross CapEx guidance of **$90–95 billion** and said net cash CapEx should be no more than **$70 billion**. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** Oracle’s FY2027 call supports a bullish OCI-AI revenue setup—large contracted RPO, accelerating deployments, very high utilization, and price renewal strength—but investors should distinguish signed backlog from near-term revenue and recognize that conversion depends on timely delivery of AI data-center capacity. [[3, 1]]
